page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7se.3xlarge is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Enhanced family. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B x86_64 processor operating at 2.9 GHz, it features 12 vCPUs derived from 6 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 24.0 GB, allocating 2.0 GB per vCPU in a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio. The CPU topology incorporates 48 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache per socket. Supported instruction extensions include AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. This instance includes no integrated local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on external block storage and providing a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates consistent middle-tier compute capabilities across synthetic and practical workloads. The stress-ng test yields a single-core score of 1870.18 and a multi-core score of 11653.27. Geekbench testing records a single-core score of 1570.0 and a multi-core score of 7822.0, with specific sub-scores including 11904.0 for software compilation via Clang and 13468.0 for ray tracing. Memory bandwidth tests reach 638.72 GB/sec for small cached reads, tapering to 82.59 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 52.05 GB/sec for uncached writes. PassMark benchmark scores include a CPU total of 16449.23, an extended instructions score of 10522.23, and a memory performance rating of 2494.91.

Application-level tests indicate strong operational throughput for web serving and key-value datastores. The server processes 11.96 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves 16.85 GB/sec static web serving throughput. For AI workloads using small 135M parameter models, LLM prompt processing reaches 1066.75 tokens per second with text generation at 239.68 tokens per second. However, medium 7B parameter model prompt processing degrades to 24.22 tokens per second, falling into the bottom 25th percentile of tested hardware. Given its 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and baseline 4 Gbps networking, the instance is well-suited for general compute tasks, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and web servers, but exhibits tradeoffs when hosting larger context LLMs or memory-intensive database engines.
